security_audit.summary: The scanner mistook Markdown backticks, fixed integrity commands, and signed descriptor data for execution or obfuscation. The workflow still installs vendor-native code with an automatic approval flag, while platform publisher signatures are not enforced.

remediation.issue: The workflow supplies the installer approval flag when the CLI is absent.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct user confirmation immediately before installation, then pass --approve-install only after that confirmation.

remediation.issue: Platform publisher signatures are deferred and disabled for bundled native binaries.
remediation.suggestion: Require a verified native signature or independently verify a signed release manifest before installing the downloaded executable.

finding_verdicts.reason: The installer uses one fixed HTTPS release URL, disables redirects, and verifies exact size plus pinned archive and executable hashes before installation.
The substitution calls fixed uname commands only to select a supported release artifact. No user-controlled command or shell expression is evaluated.
The substitution calls fixed uname solely for an operating-system check. Its result is quoted and cannot alter the executed command.
The substitution calls fixed uname solely to choose the user-local install directory. No untrusted command text is evaluated.
The quoted printf and tr pipeline removes control characters from the selected install path. This is validation, not command injection.
The quoted ls call records the install directory identity for a later race check. It does not enumerate unrelated system data.
The helper hashes the quoted existing executable before an allowlist comparison. The path is fixed under the validated install directory.
mktemp creates a unique working directory under the validated user-local target. The template and expanded path remain quoted.
The fixed wc and tr pipeline measures the downloaded archive before an exact size check. It does not evaluate user input as code.
The helper computes the archive hash for comparison with a pinned digest. This is an integrity check on a quoted path.
The fixed tar listing command inspects a hash-verified archive, and its output must match an exact three-entry allowlist before extraction.
The helper hashes the extracted executable and compares it with a pinned digest. No dynamic command is constructed.
The substitution calls fixed uname for a platform check before optional signature validation. Its output remains quoted.
The fixed codesign pipeline reads the signing identity of the quoted candidate for comparison. It does not execute candidate-controlled shell text.
The quoted ls call confirms that the install directory identity did not change. This is a race-condition defense, not reconnaissance.
The helper rehashes the quoted existing target before replacement. This prevents replacement after a concurrent change.
The installer downloads a fixed-version artifact over constrained HTTPS, then verifies exact size, archive hash, executable hash, and archive entries.
The path is the standard XDG user-local executable directory. It does not access hidden credentials or unrelated private data.
The fallback path is the standard user-local executable directory under HOME. It is the intended installation target, not sensitive hidden data.
The dot-prefixed path is a temporary installer directory created with mktemp and removed by a trap. It does not conceal persistent behavior.
The script redirects command discovery output to /dev/null while selecting a SHA-256 utility. It neither reads nor writes a sensitive device.
The script redirects command discovery output to /dev/null while selecting a SHA-256 utility. It neither reads nor writes a sensitive device.
mktemp creates a unique, quoted working directory under a validated user-local directory, and an exit trap removes it.
The hard link atomically installs the verified candidate only when the target does not exist. Failure leaves an occupied target unchanged.
The ls invocation reads only the chosen install directory inode before and after download to detect path replacement. It performs no broad reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Build an Interactive Community Onboarding Course
content.value_statement: Community guidelines often fail to give new members a clear starting path. This skill turns supplied materials into an interactive, askable PersonWise course.
actual_capabilities: Designs a structured onboarding arc from supplied community guidelines and welcome materials.
Creates and monitors interactive digital-human courses through the PersonWise CLI.
Uploads user-selected documents and tracks each source until processing completes.
Reviews course outlines, scripts, images, and factual grounding at workflow checkpoints.
Configures private or link access and returns the verified playable course URL.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser OAuth, service access, and available course credits.
Can only present policies, benefits, access levels, and norms supported by supplied materials.
Does not buy credits, broaden access, delete content, or transfer ownership without specific authorization.
Does not certify competence, guarantee platform approval, or prove real-world course completion.

use_cases.title: Welcome New Community Members
use_cases.description: Create a start-here course that explains purpose, first-week actions, spaces, rituals, rules, and support contacts.

use_cases.title: Onboard Paid Members
use_cases.description: Turn membership guides into a private course without inventing benefits, tiers, or access promises.

use_cases.title: Standardize Program Introductions
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable interactive orientation from approved program documents, branding, and event imagery.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Onboarding Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a community onboarding course from [source files]. Keep it private and use only supported facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has complete guidelines and wants a simple private course.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the First Member Week
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [page count]-page course for [community name]. Focus on first-week actions, spaces, norms, and support contacts from [sources].
prompt_templates.scenario: A community manager needs a focused activation path.

prompt_templates.title: Use Strict Source Grounding
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a materials-only onboarding course from [documents]. Include every selected source and flag any unsupported claim before publication.
prompt_templates.scenario: A regulated or policy-sensitive community needs strict grounding.

prompt_templates.title: Refine and Publish an Existing Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Review project [project ID] against [sources]. Correct factual issues, inspect visuals, preserve structure, and publish with [private or link] access.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs evidence-based revision and controlled delivery.

output_examples.input: Create a private five-page onboarding course from our handbook and welcome guide.
output: Resolved course: five pages with private access.
Sources: handbook ready; welcome guide ready.
Review: outline, script, and factual grounding completed.
Delivery: login-required course link verified as playable.

output_examples.input: Create a link-access course that explains our spaces, weekly events, and conduct rules.
output: Course arc: welcome, first actions, community spaces, weekly events, and conduct rules.
Grounding: all claims matched the supplied materials.
Access: link sharing enabled and the playable URL verified.

output_examples.input: Update the existing course after our moderation contacts changed.
output_examples.output: The support contacts were updated from the new policy document. Course structure stayed unchanged, and the private course was verified.

best_practices: Supply current guidelines, welcome materials, contact details, and approved branding before course creation.
State the desired page count and access mode, or accept the private default.
Review factual checkpoints and resolve unsupported claims before publishing or sharing.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent benefits, rules, testimonials, member counts, or access tiers.
Do not upload agent-discovered local files without reviewing the exact path and purpose.
Do not treat a private editor URL as a public share link.

faq.question: What materials should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide community guidelines, welcome documents, program details, support contacts, and approved images that learners should see.

faq.question: Can the skill create a course without documents?
faq.answer: Yes, it can create from a supplied topic or text. It must still avoid unsupported community-specific claims.

faq.question: Is the course public by default?
faq.answer: No. The workflow defaults to private access unless you request link access or another publication target.

faq.question: Does this use community course credits?
faq.answer: Yes. A creation request authorizes the required existing credit, but the skill never purchases credits automatically.

faq.question: Can learners ask questions during the course?
faq.answer: Yes. PersonWise courses support voice questions grounded in the course content and supplied sources.

faq.question: What software and account access are required?
faq.answer: You need a compatible PersonWise CLI, browser OAuth access, an eligible account, and available service capacity.
